items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 17, overrideLimiter=true — parsed fresh from the 1.21.11 ParticleTypes <clinit>) with a dedicated ElderGuardianParticle$Provider (ParticleResources.registerProviders, offsets 296-300) and spawns it on game event GUARDIAN_ELDER_EFFECT (ClientPacketListener.handleGameEvent, offset 544; addParticle at the player position, offset 554, plus the curse sound at 598 — all re-read from the 1.21.11 client jar, same offsets as 1.21.10). The port's ParticleType enum (125 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets (lan_particles.rs:491), /particle rejects it (particle.notFound, world_cmds.rs:718), and override_limiter() misses it (28 vanilla vs 27 real-1.21.11 Rust entries; the Rust list's 4 extra entries are the dead geyser types). The providers driver does NOT send elder_guardian cases (omitted from the 126-kind set), so the defect blocks no driver here — it silently skips the type. The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime, mob_blocks.rs:87/96), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

items.evidence: Particle::read decodes wire id 42 (flash, verified against the 1.21.11 registry — id 41 in 1.21.7, 42 here as in 1.21.10) as Color(i32) — a flash particle always carries a colour — but hub_particle has no Flash arm in its Color match (EntityEffect | TintedLeaves only, lan_particles.rs:440), so the packet is built with data None and Particle::write (:297, writes data by presence, not id: `let Some(data) = &self.data else { return }`) emits the id with no colour bytes; guests reading id 42 consume the next 4 stream bytes as the colour and desync. Reachable only via /particle flash on a LAN host (cmd_particle builds ParticleOptions::simple(ty) via the catch-all, world_cmds.rs:829; Flash is otherwise created client-side only, in firework explosions, particles.rs:3785); the local player draws directly and is unaffected.
items.title: /particle minecraft:flash sends a malformed packet to LAN guests (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 registers SPRUCE_LEAVES as TintedParticleLeavesBlock with leafParticleChance 0.01 (Blocks.<clinit> parsed fresh for 1.21.11 with the class-file parser — 'spruce_leaves' -> lambda$static$36 -> TintedParticleLeavesBlock(0.01F), same lambda number as 1.21.10; LeavesBlock.animateTick rolls nextFloat() < chance). The port maps spruce_leaves to Animate::Leaves(None, None, false) — no falling particle (animate_tick.rs:151). All 10 other leaf blocks match vanilla (cherry 0.1, pale oak 0.02, rest tinted 0.01; azalea fixed colour -9399763 matches the port's 0x70922D). The marker driver would fail its spruce zoo cases (oracle emits, probe emits none — the probe runs the port's real animate_tick, marker_particles_probe.rs:168); the driver's own comment ('the spruce that never falls', test_marker_particles_parity.py:114) encodes the same wrong belief and needs correcting with the fix.
items.title: Spruce leaves never drop falling-leaf particles (recurs from 1.21.7; reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11 has no SpeleothemBlock class at all (0 entries in either jar; PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly) and no speleothems tag in either jar's datapack. Vanilla LevelEventHandler routes 1504 to PointedDripstoneBlock.spawnDripParticle with no class gate (offset 3519, verified fresh). The client routes 1504 to dripstone_drip_particle (game.rs:4377), whose first act is the is_stalactite gate (level_particles.rs:243-244): has_class("SpeleothemBlock") is false for every block in 1.21.11, so the drip particle never spawns. The ambient animateTick drip path is unaffected (name-based table, animate_tick.rs:397-410; 0.12 roll, same-block climb, 0.02 cauldron rule all match vanilla). Whether the port's server actually transfers fluid to cauldrons in 1.21.11 (G6's status) is Batch 5's scope; the client gate is dead regardless.
items.title: Level-event 1504 stalactite drip particle never fires: is_stalactite gates on SpeleothemBlock, absent in 1.21.11 (reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's ParticleGroup.add is a plain queue add into an EvictingQueue.create(16384) (javap -c on the 1.21.11 client jar: particles.add(p); the queue itself is an EvictingQueue, constructor offsets 5-8) — when the queue is full the OLDEST particle is evicted to make room for the new one. There is no size check and no probability roll in add; the cap is enforced by eviction, not rejection. Same vanilla form as 1.21.10. The 1.21.11 port's tick_tracking (particles.rs:3888, the drain that moves every created particle from pending into the live list — create() pushes to pending, :2098) enforces the 26.2 form (:3933-3945): at 16,384 live particles every new particle is dropped, and above 12,288 new particles are dropped with probability 1 - ((16384-size)/4096)^2, drawing the level random for each rejection (constant at :1358-1359). The port's behaviour matches neither vanilla 1.21.11 (evict oldest) nor vanilla 26.1.2 (plain queue, no cap at all). The cap only bites in particle-heavy scenes (above 12,288 live particles); below that threshold the port matches vanilla exactly. The repair here is evict-oldest, not the 26.1 tree's cap removal.
items.title: Particle engine drops new particles at the 16,384 cap (with probabilistic thinning above 12,288); vanilla 1.21.11 evicts the oldest instead

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect is a record with ONE field (diameter: float) — no directional_particles field — and its apply calls LivingEntity.randomTeleport(x, y, z, true), which broadcasts entity event 46 (128 portal particles at the entity; LivingEntity.handleEntityEvent case 46, offsets 201/208, PORTAL at 389, addParticle at 407; broadcast at bipush 46, offset 177). Vanilla LevelEventHandler has NO 2017 case (79-case lookupswitch). The 1.21.11 tree carries the 26.3 form: TeleportConsume has a directional_particles: bool field (teleport_consume.rs:6); items.rs:157-160 reads it from data with unwrap_or(true), and the 1.21.11 data never carries the field (chorus_fruit consumable is {"on_consume_effects": [{"type": "minecraft:teleport_randomly"}]}; 0 occurrences of directional_particles in the datagen items.json), so it defaults to true; teleport_consume.rs:109-121 fires the event on every successful teleport and the client impl (consume.rs:422-431) calls level_event_at(2017, ...), routed (game.rs:4338-4341) to consume_teleport_particles -> block_teleportation ([127,127,127], particles.rs:1859), 128 portal particles along the old->new line. The port ALSO fires the vanilla-correct event 46 (consume.rs:188-194, remote.rs:4774-4777), so a chorus-fruit teleport shows BOTH the correct burst AND a second, wrong directional trail. The 26.1 tree has no directional_particles anywhere.
items.title: Chorus fruit shows an extra 2017 directional teleport trail vanilla never sends, on top of the correct event-46 burst (26.3-form; the 26.1 tree has no such event)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's EnderMan.teleport calls randomTeleport(x, y, z, true) (offset 110) -> entity event 46 -> 128 portal particles at the entity; the only addParticle call in EnderMan is the ambient aiStep emission, not the teleport. LevelEventHandler has NO 2018 case. The 26.1 tree's mobs/enderman.rs documents this explicitly ('26.3 also fires the level event 2018 portal trail; 26.1 has no such event here'). The 1.21.11 tree's teleport_to (mobs/enderman.rs:80; event 46 at :160-166, 2018 send at :174-184) pushes BOTH the vanilla-correct entity event 46 AND MobEvent::LevelEvent { id: 2018, ... } (when not silent), routed (game.rs:4343-4346) to enderman_teleport_particles -> enderman_teleportation (particles.rs:1884), 128 portal particles along the old->new line. items.title: Enderman teleport shows an extra 2018 directional portal trail vanilla never sends, on top of the correct event-46 burst (26.3-form; the 26.1 tree omits it)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's Shulker.teleportSomewhere does: unRide, setAttachFace, playSound(SHULKER_TELEPORT), setPos, gameEvent(TELEPORT), set peek data, setTarget — no randomTeleport, no addParticle, no broadcastEntityEvent, no level event anywhere in the class (0 such references in the full javap -c dump, 1.21.11 server-game jar). A shulker teleport in vanilla shows zero particles. LevelEventHandler has NO 2016 case. The port's mobs/shulker.rs:366-371 pushes MobEvent::LevelEvent { id: 2016, ... } on every teleport. In the 26.1 tree this event is dropped (game.rs has no 2016 arm), so the 26.1 port accidentally matches vanilla. The 1.21.11 tree keeps the handler (game.rs:4333-4336 -> shulker_teleport_particles -> block_teleportation [8,8,8], particles.rs:1859), so every shulker teleport now shows 128 portal particles along the old->new line that vanilla never shows. Unlike G06/G07 there is no correct event-46 burst underneath — the trail is the ONLY particle output and it is entirely wrong.
items.title: Shulker teleport shows a 2016 directional trail; vanilla shows NO particles at all (the 26.1 tree drops the event and accidentally matches vanilla)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.11's MultiPlayerGameMode never calls addBreakingBlockEffect anywhere in the class (0 occurrences in the full javap -c dump), and LevelEventHandler has NO 2019/2020 cases. startDestroyBlock plays nothing and spawns nothing; continueDestroyBlock plays ONLY the hit sound, on destroy ticks 0, 4, 8, ... (destroyTicks % 4.0 == 0, volume (volume+1)/8, pitch * 0.5, offsets 199-208) — no particle at any point while digging. The 1.21.11 tree keeps the 26.2 form: breaking_block_effects (level_particles.rs:353-373: hit sound when play_sound, plus crack_particle — one crumb on the mined face), called from startDestroyBlock (remote.rs:8171, breaking_block_effects(hit.pos, hit.face, true)). The port's server never sends 2019/2020, so the network dispatch (game.rs:4298-4306) is dead and the continue path plays NOTHING. Net effect vs vanilla: an extra crack particle + a hit sound at the first hit (vanilla: silence), then silence for the rest of the dig (vanilla: a hit sound every 4th tick). The 26.1 tree is correct here (start plays nothing; continue plays sound-only on ticks 1, 5, 9, ...). The particle half (extra crumb) is minted here; the sound-schedule half is flagged for Batch 10.
items.title: Digging shows a crack particle (and a mistimed hit sound) vanilla never shows; the every-fourth-tick hit sound is missing (26.2-form breaking effects; the 26.1 tree is sound-only)

items.evidence: Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh here. Vanilla 1.21.11's SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe (javap -c, 1.21.11 server-game jar) is y < maxY && !state.liquid() && !state.is(BlockTags.FIRE) — no teleport tag. The #entities_can_teleport_to tag does not exist in 1.21.11: 0 entries in either jar's datapack (verified by jar listing; the tag is a 26.2 addition). The port's spread_safe (world_cmds.rs:2091-2114) returns y < max_y && !liquid && teleportable, where teleportable (:2100-2109) requires membership in #entities_can_teleport_to — always false in 1.21.11. So spread_safe is ALWAYS false; in the spread loop (:1978-1986) every collision-free iteration re-randomizes every point, collisions stays true, and the loop runs until iteration >= 10_000, when the command fails with commands.spreadplayers.failed.entities (or .teams, :1991-1999). /spreadplayers cannot succeed in the 1.21.11 port on any terrain. Commands-area; minted here on the coordinator's routing via Batch 7 — the merge may re-route it to Batch 9's ledger.
items.method: javap + data + source (Batch 7-routed flag, verified fresh)
items.title: /spreadplayers always fails: spread_safe requires the #entities_can_teleport_to tag, which 1.21.11 does not have (Batch 7-routed; reproduces from 26.1.2 and 1.21.10)

method: Static analysis only (no driver runs, no cargo tests, no commits — per the batch brief; no prepared 1.21.11 data exists in the worktree, so data checks used the datagen reports). Every vanilla claim was javap-verified fresh against 1.21.11's own named jars (client-named + server-game-named, sha1-verified; the bundler server.jar was never javap'd): LevelEventHandler lookupswitch (79-case main switch, 82 distinct, no 2015-2020, no 1053/1054), ParticleGroup.add (EvictingQueue.create(16384)), MultiPlayerGameMode (0 addBreakingBlockEffect calls, 4th-tick hit sound), LivingEntity.randomTeleport/handleEntityEvent (event 46 -> 128 PORTAL), Shulker.teleportSomewhere (0 particle/event refs), EnderMan.teleport (event 46), DragonEggBlock.teleport (128 lerped PORTAL), SpreadPlayersCommand.Position.isSafe (y < maxY && !liquid && !is(FIRE)), LocalPlayer ctor (7 args), ServerLevel ctor (11 args with RandomSequences), TextureAtlasSprite ctor (protected 7-arg), Holder$Reference (no bindComponents), ParticleTypes <clinit> parsed from the javap -c dump (115 registrations, 28 limiter-true; limiter boolean read as the iconst AFTER the name ldc), ParticleResources provider registration, ClientPacketListener game event, TeleportRandomlyConsumeEffect record shape, oracle APIs, Nautilus/ZombieNautilus/CamelHusk superclass chains (inherited 6/7/18 bursts). Registry census from 1.21.11's own datagen registries.json (115 particle types, ids contiguous 0-114 — identical names + ids to 1.21.10; 157 entity types, +4 vs 1.21.10: nautilus, zombie_nautilus, camel_husk, parched). Leaf registrations parsed fresh from the 1.21.11 Blocks.<clinit> with the 1.21.10 batch's class-file parser re-run unmodified. Source comparison against versions/1.21.11/crates/; data checks against the 1.21.11 datagen reports (registries.json, blocks.json, items.json) and the jar datapacks. Oracle triage from this batch's own javac measurement (single-file compiles with JDK 25 on the 'both' classpath: both named jars + 1.21.11's own 107 game library jars, downloaded from Mojang per version.json and sha1-verified, + jsr305) — Batch 0's measured table had not landed when this batch ran, so the coordinator should reconcile against it when it does. JDK 25 vs JDK 21 note: JDK 25 reports cascading errors JDK 21 suppresses (providers 19 vs 7, same root causes); counts here are the JDK 25 counts, comparable to the 1.21.10 run's. The Batch 7-routed /spreadplayers flag was verified fresh (javap + data + source) and minted as B8-G10.

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 8 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: all 115 particle types, emitters, providers; 8 drivers found in the tree (7 particle-named + effect_sync, particle-adjacent; the plan claims 9, the 9th is unaccounted for). DRAFT: not committed — checks + triage only per the batch brief. All ten 1.21.10 behaviour defects reproduce in 1.21.11 itself (the template is where they live), and all three 1.21.7 items reproduce. Three re-checks split on vanilla changes between 1.21.10 and 1.21.11: the nautilus family arrived (B8-H05 WITHDRAWN — nautilus cases are legitimate checks now; B8-H04 REVERSED — zombie_nautilus/camel_husk omissions are a live gap again) and the 26.x entity subpackages, world.attribute package, jspecify and 7-arg TextureAtlasSprite ctor arrived (B8-O04 emitter and B8-O05 entity oracles FIXED — they compile clean; the five still-broken oracles fail with far fewer errors: 33 total vs 92 for 1.21.10). No new behaviour defects beyond the re-checks. The 26.1-record corrections are carried (H02 counts cases()-yielded kinds; the entity-API attribution to LivingEntity; B8-G10 checked fresh). Oracle verdicts rest on this batch's own javac measurement because Batch 0's table had not landed.
systemic_note: The template is where the defects live: all ten behaviour defects reproduce in 1.21.11 itself, verified fresh — the 1.21.10 child inherited them unchanged. The five 26.2/26.3-form reversions (B8-G05–G09) are the template's own, and the 26.1 tree remains the repair reference for four of them (for B8-G05 the repair is evict-oldest, not cap-removal — vanilla 1.21.11's EvictingQueue form, same as 1.21.10's). The directional-teleport events are one feature in three defects: 2017/2018 ADD a trail on top of the correct event-46 burst (double particles), while 2016 is pure invention (vanilla shows no particles for a shulker teleport at all). Vanilla 1.21.11 moved halfway to 26.x, and the oracle problem shrank with it: 5 of 8 particle oracles fail (33 errors) vs 7 of 8 (92 errors) for 1.21.10, because vanilla adopted the 26.x entity subpackages, the world.attribute package, jspecify, the 7-arg TextureAtlasSprite ctor, the monster.zombie package and the effect methods — leaving only the genuinely-26.x-only residue (geyser, BlockStateModelSet, ItemStackTemplate, sprite Material, the 26.x ServerLevel/LocalPlayer call forms, bindComponents). The nautilus family arrival flips two harness verdicts at once: nautilus cases become legitimate checks (H05 withdrawn) while the zombie_nautilus/camel_husk omission becomes a live gap again (H04 reversed). The positive systemic finding stands: the port's particle tables are otherwise exact — all 115 types covered end-to-end except elder_guardian, all 18 data-carrying wire ids correct, all 28 limiter flags correct except elder_guardian, all 30 entity-burst pairs and all 45 marker-zoo blocks covered, and all 11 leaf blocks' chances verified — the gaps are narrow and enumerated, not a broad drift. The 11 extra types in the Rust enum are dead but unreachable.
